clue.text: Network supplying power brand of vehicle

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
Lexus is a car brand, Toyota's luxury marque

explanation.surface: A grid of power lines feeding electricity to a particular make of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A plexus is an interwoven web, especially of nerves or blood vessels, so it is a kind of network.

clue.text: Soldier's nothing left to provide cover

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper; with the 's the word becomes PARAS
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: A trooper with nothing remaining to give him protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, giving shade or shelter from sunlight.

clue.text: I'm pierced, suffering in outer layer of skin

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are hurt and twisted out of shape, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a piercing complains of pain in their outer skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermic is the adjective for the epidermis, the surface tissue of the body.

clue.text: One-off HE establishment — what you get in Paris

parts.note: HE is higher education, and a uni is a university
que is French for what

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind university, and the French experience you get there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique is the only one of its kind, a singular item.

clue.text: Attempt to restrict one cunning form of government by a few

definitions.text: form of government by a few

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the attempt word closes around the other letters

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral for one
arch means sly or knowingly cunning

explanation.surface: Someone trying to curb a single crafty oligarchy, a political theorist's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A triarchy is rule by three people, a small handful sharing power.

clue.text: Beginning to be a fine England cricketer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an origin or source
second meaning: Joe ..., England batsman and former captain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like the start of a sporting career, but the two halves are separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A root is where something starts, and Joe Root is a leading English Test batsman.

clue.text: After drink a Conservative becomes unpredictable

indicators.note: after places the Conservative letters following the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician grows erratic once the beer has flowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on chance, from Latin alea, a die, so it is random.

clue.text: East End gangster brothers reportedly in frenzy

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what is heard said, not written, gives the letters

parts.note: the Krays were twin brothers who ran organised crime in London's East End in the 1960s

explanation.surface: Notorious London criminals rumoured to be in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a passing mania or fad, a wild enthusiasm.

clue.text: By Jove, fellow's travelling north some distance!

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: egad is an old exclamation of surprise, like 'by Jove'
Ray is a man's name, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a man has headed a long way north.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a length measured in yards, as in a golf hole or football gain.

clue.text: Restrict soldiers at home repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for at home is written out twice in a row

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Keeping troops confined to barracks again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to hold back or curb, as a rider pulls the reins on a horse.

clue.text: Aim of those dyeing hair? Let's not be nasty!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: going blonde, the goal of bleaching one's hair
second meaning: the everyday phrase used to be even-handed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense takes 'fair' as light-coloured hair; the second is the stock phrase meaning 'to be just about it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to concede a point generously, and literally names the wish to have blonde hair.

clue.text: Orange transport for conveying book collection

indicators.note: conveying here means holding, so the transport word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to carry is to transport
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tangerine-coloured vehicle used to ferry a library's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroty describes an orange-red shade like a carrot, often of hair.

clue.text: Like a mirror offering great views maybe — but no cat reflected in it!

indicators.note: no here means without, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: spectacular describes a view that is a great sight

indicators.note: reflected means the word cat is read backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a looking glass that shows a splendid scene, but no cat can be seen in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SPECTACULAR and remove TAC, the word cat turned round, which sits in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Specular means mirror-like or relating to reflection, from Latin speculum, a mirror.

clue.text: Emerging from Thessalonica, the national goddess

indicators.note: Emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A national deity rising out of the Greek city of Thessalonica.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Actress cutting final performance short

indicators.note: cutting says a letter is removed from the performance word
short says the word stops one letter early, losing its end

parts.note: a swan song is a last performance before retiring

explanation.surface: A performer trimming her farewell show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood film star, best known for Sunset Boulevard.

clue.text: Fruit something squishy? Chop off front bit

indicators.note: chopping off the front bit removes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: slime is soft, squishy stuff

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit gone soft, with its bruised end sliced away.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime is a small green citrus fruit.

clue.text: One's often raised game after inconclusive result

indicators.note: after places the game word following the result word

parts.note: a draw is a game with no winner
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A rematch called for after a tied contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a castle bridge hinged so it can be lifted to block entry.

clue.text: People who are a bit too 'sugary'?

definitions.text: People who are a bit too 'sugary'?

parts.words: People who are a bit too 'sugary'?
parts.note: sugary is taken literally: these people have too much sugar in the blood, not too sweet a manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugary' looks like it means sickly-sweet in character; the quotation marks and question mark hint it is meant literally about blood sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Those with this condition have raised glucose levels in the blood.

clue.text: Search with soldiers to get hold of a Roman official

indicators.note: to get hold of is to grip, so the outer letters close round the other one

parts.note: a quest is a search
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A hunt with troops to seize a magistrate of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaestor was a Roman magistrate in charge of public finances.

clue.text: Ultimately you cannot act badly as someone dealing with money

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of you

explanation.surface: A finance professional who simply cannot behave poorly, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant keeps and checks financial records for a living.

clue.text: Said everything with nasty edge

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are spoilt, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spoke every word with a cutting tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means claimed or stated without proof, as in an alleged offence.

clue.text: Post — preserve with touch of bitumen

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve

indicators.note: a touch of something is just a little, here its first letter

parts.note: first letter of bitumen

explanation.surface: A wooden post treated with a little tar to keep it sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the upright post at the side of a door or window frame.

clue.text: One that's charged with infliction of violence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... stores electric charge
second meaning: ... is the crime of unlawful physical attack, as in assault and ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person accused of assault; 'charged' turns out to mean electrically.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery holds a store of electrical energy, and the legal sense is an unlawful beating.

clue.text: Noisy festivities including a show

indicators.note: including says the festivities word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: a revel is lively, noisy merrymaking

explanation.surface: A loud party that features a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or expose, making something visible.

clue.text: After deficiency, you set about servant

indicators.note: after places the turned word following the deficiency word

parts.note: a lack is a shortage

indicators.note: set about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Short of staff, someone lays into a manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a footman or servile follower who does another's bidding.

clue.text: Political groups providing money, mostly to accommodate politician

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the trimmed money word holds the other letters
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: cash is money
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Factions funding a lawmaker by putting him up.
explanation.definitionFit: Camps are factions or sides holding a shared view, as in the rival camps of a party.

clue.text: In a little time gather very English group to support cause

indicators.note: to gather is to take in, so the time word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a moment is a brief time

explanation.surface: Rounding up a very English band of campaigners in a spare minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement is an organised campaign of people working for a shared aim, such as the labour movement.

clue.text: Enthusiastic knight moving forward? This is bent before monarch

indicators.note: moving forward says the knight's letter is shifted nearer the front of the word

parts.note: keen means eager or enthusiastic
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: An eager knight advancing to kneel before the king.
explanation.definitionFit: One kneels before royalty, bending the joint of the leg in homage.

clue.text: Omen gets mistaken for precious object

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sign of fortune misread as a valuable treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone is a jewel, a cut mineral valued for its beauty and rarity.

clue.text: Punishment for caging the Spanish moggy?

indicators.note: caging means enclosing, so the punishment word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a fine is a monetary punishment
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A penalty for locking up a Spanish cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A moggy is British slang for an ordinary house cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means a cat or member of the cat family, used here as a noun for a pet.

clue.text: Spies little fellow and expresses sorrow

parts.note: Des is a short form of the name Desmond
to cry is to show grief

explanation.surface: Secret agents watch a small man who is weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of something distant, so it means spots or sees.

clue.text: Garish old carriage with wooden interior

indicators.note: interior says the wooden word goes inside the carriage word

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn hired carriage
ash is a wood, so wooden stands for it

explanation.surface: A gaudy antique carriage fitted out inside with timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy means showy and ostentatious, as is something garish.
